notes:
An official legal procedure conducted when the cause of death is unclear. In Japan, {検視|けんし} is performed by a prosecutor or police officer (not a medical doctor) to determine whether foul play is involved. If further medical examination is needed, it leads to {司法|しほう}{解剖|かいぼう} (judicial autopsy).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {検視|けんし}を{行|おこな}う: to conduct an inquest
- {検視|けんし}{官|かん}: coroner, medical examiner
- {検視|けんし}{報告|ほうこく}: inquest report
- {検視|けんし}の{結果|けっか}: results of the inquest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {検死|けんし}: postmortem examination — variant writing, often used interchangeably but technically less formal
- {司法|しほう}{解剖|かいぼう}: judicial autopsy — a more thorough medical procedure ordered when foul play is suspected
- {解剖|かいぼう}: autopsy, dissection — the medical procedure itself

definitions.explanation: an official examination of a dead body to determine the cause and circumstances of death, conducted by legal authorities

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}が{検視|けんし}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The police conducted a coroner's inquest.

examples.japanese: {検視|けんし}の{結果|けっか}、{事件性|じけんせい}はないと{判断|はんだん}された。
examples.english: As a result of the inquest, it was determined there was no criminal involvement.

examples.japanese: {不審|ふしん}{死|し}の{場合|ばあい}は{必|かなら}ず{検視|けんし}が{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: In the case of a suspicious death, a coroner's examination is always conducted.
